The Amended PDP8 prioritizes and encourages the development of biomass power and waste-to-energy by using agricultural and forestry by-products to promote afforestation and otherwise address environmental issues.

### Success Fee-Based Brokerage Model

Prassas Capital, a firm that has repeatedly secured financing for biogas developers across several projects throughout the country, operates on a success fee basis with no monthly retainer required. This is a notable example of the broker/intermediary revenue model in the WTE space.

### Challenges for Brokers & Intermediaries

Many private equity firms in alternative energy claim interest in waste-to-energy, but what they really want is wind and solar. Few financial investors understand the technology and operating risks behind WTE, and are ultimately unwilling to close.

Waste-to-energy and recycling projects have a high failure rate, which has an enormous influence on the reception by lenders and third-party equity providers.

### Critical Project Development Requirements

Viable projects require long-term feedstock and offtake agreements, and merchant facilities are exponentially more difficult to finance. Unlevered project IRR of high teens to mid-twenties is necessary to attract private equity.

The project needs an EPC with the financial capacity to offer performance guarantees, the operator must be able to demonstrate ongoing operating capability, and a technology is proven when it can operate on a commercial scale.

### Revenue Streams for WTE Projects

The mechanism of returning investments is based on the tariff for energy produced. Waste-to-energy projects have three mechanisms for returning investments: energy tariff, tipping fee, and, sometimes, carbon credits.

In Europe, waste-to-energy projects require feed-in-tariff (FIT) and tipping fee (TF), with FIT for major countries at 0.12–0.14 USD per kWh and an additional tipping fee of 80–100 USD per ton.

### Consulting & Development Service Models

WTEI develops comprehensive feasibility studies for investors, advises clients on ideal plant size, location and infrastructure, and has a pool of international investors in the UK and Gulf countries interested in WTE investments with government-guaranteed revenue streams.

Their services include arranging financial and organizational structuring, supporting creation of local project SPVs, performing construction supervision, providing guarantees of final output and declared IRR level, and consulting investors during the operating period.

### Financing Landscape

Generally speaking, lenders are not comfortable with waste-to-energy on a project finance basis — smaller lenders don't understand them, while larger lenders are only interested in projects greater than $50–75 million from larger clients.

Developers must navigate numerous uncertainties including technological risks, regulatory changes, and community concerns, and the initial stages of project development often require substantial capital investment before revenue generation begins.
